summary: The ReportQueue module manages the selection, filtering, status updates, email delivery, and deletion of print jobs (reports) for users within an ASP.NET web application. It is implemented as a page and as a user control, allowing staff to interact with queued reports using a rich UI that supports filtering, batch actions, and feedback via warnings and errors.
purpose: To provide users (primarily staff) the ability to view, filter, select, act upon, and manage print jobs (reports). This includes marking reports as delivered or undelivered, emailing reports to default or specific recipients, permanently deleting reports, and refreshing the report queue view.

workflows.name: Standard Report View and Action Workflow
steps: User loads the ReportQueue view. If first load, sets up session and filters.
User applies filters using checkboxes and dropdowns (report type, staff, status).
Report list is displayed (using rprReportQ, dsReportQ) with the ability to select individual or all reports (cmdSelectAll/cmdSelectNone).
User selects one or more reports and chooses an action: Mark as delivered, Undelivered, Email (default/specific recipient), or Delete.
Actions are processed; status is updated accordingly in backend via PrintJobs.PrintJobSetStatus or PrintJobs.PrintJobDelete.
If emailing, the appropriate email popup or batch process is triggered. If deleting, confirmation may be shown before removal.
View is refreshed to display updated report queue state.
Feedback for errors or warnings is shown in panels as needed.

workflows.name: Report Email Workflow
steps: User selects reports and chooses to email (default or specific).
System verifies at least one report is selected and recipient(s) are valid.
If validation passes, builds URL to EmailPopup.aspx and uses PageMethods.hashURL for security.
On success, opens popup window for the email process.

business_rules: Only reports that are not marked as 'Submitted' and have an available output file can be marked as delivered, emailed, or deleted.
Delete action may be hidden if the selected staff user does not match the current session user.
Email action validation ensures each report has a default or specific recipient before sending; otherwise, a message is shown.
Selection actions (All/None) and report-specific actions are managed by client-side scripts and server-side code.
validations: On email actions, checks for at least one report selected and validates recipient assignment; otherwise, alerts the user.
On batch actions, only processes selected reports with valid IDs.
Further validations on state transitions (e.g., from undelivered to delivered) are enforced in PrintJobs backend.
calculations: Counts of reports by category (delivered/not delivered/other) are calculated and displayed in summary labels.
Dynamic building and maintenance of client-side lists for selected reports, recipient IDs, and group indices.
conditions: UI elements (such as Delete action) may be hidden based on session user context.
Group summaries and warning/error panels are only shown if applicable reports exist or an error/warning state occurs.
system_behavior: AJAX and postback are used to maintain state and update the UI after actions.
Repeater (rprReportQ) binds to an ObjectDataSource (dsReportQ) with filters provided by the user.
Client-side JavaScript is injected dynamically to support batch selection, email popups, and UI toggling.
Summary and category counts update in real time as the view changes.
dependencies: HSPnet.DataLayer.PrintJobs for backend data access and actions.
UserSession for session management and user context.
ASP.NET Events (Page_Load, Page_PreRender, OnItemDataBound, OnItemCommand, etc.)
Client-side JavaScript for dynamic UI updates and validation.
exceptions: Display of error/warning panels if operations fail or invalid data is detected (e.g., no recipient assigned for email, no report selected, backend exceptions).
content_gaps: No details about the PrintJobs.PrintJobSetStatus or PrintJobs.PrintJobDelete backend methods implementation.
Some referenced resources (like text for UI labels) are dynamically localized and not provided.
Assumes a specific session and user management infrastructure exists.
